title: I built an automated macro & swing-trading terminal inside Discord — looking for honest feedback from technical/macro traders (Free Day One Beta)
author: Late-Pattern6450
selftext:
Hey everyone,

For the past few months I’ve been building Stocky — an automated market-intelligence and swing-trading terminal inside Discord: [https://stocky.trading](https://stocky.trading)

The goal is simple: give retail traders institutional-grade market context and structured trade tracking in one clean workspace, without having to pay $100+/mo across five different subscriptions.

While the terminal started with US equities and macro breadth, a huge part of the engine is built around macro catalysts, real-time news flow, and strict technical risk management:

• Live Macro & Market Intelligence: Automated macro data releases, real-time breaking news feeds, and broader market regime/breadth tracking (risk-on vs. risk-off context).

• Structured Swing Scanner & Tracking: Automated EOD setups with clear entry, stop-loss, and target levels tracked automatically.

• On-Demand Technical & Fundamental Breakdowns: Slash commands (/analyze, /earnings, /fund) that pull clean multi-timeframe technicals, relative strength, and key levels in seconds.

Where we are right now (Day One Beta):

We just opened our Day One Founders Beta (100% free) and are looking for our very first active members. I don’t want to build this in a vacuum — the whole point is to grow with the community and let early traders shape what gets built next.

If you trade macro, indices, or swing setups and want to test the terminal or roast the setup, you can grab a free Day One Beta pass directly here: [https://stocky.trading](https://stocky.trading)

Would genuinely love any honest feedback on the layout, signal structure, or what you’d want to see added.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: honest one: the auto-tracked stop and target is the bit I'd check first. on a daily bar that touches both, which one does it count? most trackers quietly pick the target and the hit rate looks better than it was. I'd show that rule right next to the stats.

replies.author: Late-Pattern6450
replies.body:
Super fair point—intra-bar ambiguity is one of the easiest ways trackers quietly juice their win rates, so calling that out is spot on.

Because the bot runs live intraday checks rather than purely end-of-day OHLC batching, real-time price action normally resolves which level hit first. That said, for any edge case where both levels get tagged within the same evaluation window (or on a gap/wick), the only honest rule is conservative tie-breaking—counting the stop-loss first rather than assuming the best-case fill.

Displaying that exact resolution rule right next to the stats is a great call. Adding that label directly to the tracker output so anyone looking at the numbers sees the methodology upfront.

Appreciate the honest feedback—if you ever want to stress-test the scanner or tracker logic directly, the free beta pass is linked above.
